photos.title: Oceanfront towers in Myrtle Beach, USGS oblique aerial photo, August 24, 2011
photos.what: A row of oceanfront high-rise and mid-rise buildings in Myrtle Beach seen from a plane over the ocean: flat roofs with rooftop boxes, stacked balconies on every floor, pools and umbrellas behind the dunes, the beach and surf in front, parking lots and trees behind. People on the beach are too small to recognize.
photos.caption: Oceanfront towers in Myrtle Beach, seen from a plane over the ocean in 2011.
photos.alt: A row of oceanfront towers in Myrtle Beach with flat roofs, stacked balconies and pools behind the dunes, seen from a plane over the ocean
photos.author: U.S. Geological Survey
photos.credit: Photo: U.S. Geological Survey, public domain. Credit not required; give it anyway.
photos.provenance: U.S. government photo: USGS baseline coastal oblique aerial survey 11CCH03 (Ponte Vedra, Florida, to the South Carolina/North Carolina border), flown 2011-08-24, photographer Karen L.M. Morgan (USGS). Frame 2011_0824_180052d.jpg from https://coastal.er.usgs.gov/data-release/doi-F7N877XX/data/11CCH03_0824_180000.zip; aircraft position 33.699958 N, 78.862068 W (11CCH03-Photolocations.csv; the position of the plane, not of the buildings). Data release: Morgan, K.L.M., 2017, https://doi.org/10.5066/F7N877XX. The same release as the photos on /hoa/special-assessments/ and /sell/out-of-state-buyers/ (different frames).
photos.license_note: USGS metadata, Use_Constraints: 'Public domain data from the U.S. Government are freely redistributable with proper metadata and source attribution. Please recognize the U.S. Geological Survey as the originator of the dataset.'
photos.subject_check: Looked at full size by the writer on 2026-11-01. The frame shows oceanfront towers with flat roofs and stacked balconies; it does not show whether each building is a condo or a hotel, so the caption says 'oceanfront towers', names no building, and says only that roofs and balconies like these are parts a condo reserve fund saves for. No sign or name is legible at page size. Reused on /buyers/va-loans/ (2026-11-02, looked at full size again): the caption there says these are oceanfront towers, names no building, and says only how few oceanfront resort buildings in our directory have an accepted VA record.

photos.crop_note: Cut as a 16x9 band from the 3008x1960 frame (rows 230 to 1922), then resized; 1x1, 4x3 and 16x9 crops from its center for the share image

photos.title: Exhibit at Warbird Park, Myrtle Beach (Carol M. Highsmith, 2017)
photos.what: Warbird Park in Myrtle Beach: military jets on display on a round plaza with small plaques, under tall pines.
photos.caption: Warbird Park in Myrtle Beach.
photos.alt: Military jets painted in camouflage on display on a round plaza with small plaques, under tall pine trees at Warbird Park in Myrtle Beach
photos.original_size: 8688x3940 (Library of Congress TIFF); every file is from the Library's 50% rendering (4344x1970)
photos.provenance: Carol M. Highsmith's America Project, Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division, LC-DIG-highsm-43994. Downloaded from the Library's IIIF service (tile.loc.gov, service:pnp:highsm:43900:43994) on 2026-11-02, at 25% and 50%. The record of batch 2026-10-b (data/2026-10-b/photos.json) was the first use; its files never reached the site, so this page carries its own. The aircraft are display pieces, not artwork, and no person is in the frame. Cropped to 16:9 from the left, leaving out a fourth jet at the far left edge.
photos.author: Carol M. Highsmith
photos.credit: Photo: Carol M. Highsmith, public domain, via the Library of Congress. Credit not required; give it anyway.

photos.subject_check: Looked at full size by the writer on 2026-11-02: three jets (one on a pedestal at the left), plaques on stone stands, a round brick plaza, pines and parked cars behind. No person is recognizable. No sign is the subject. The caption says only that this is Warbird Park and that the park keeps the base's history (ledger row 37).
